The Doomsday Clock

By: Eugene Botha | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
....the doomsday clock that shows how far humanity is from selfdestruction

Unique Selling Point:
A physical metaphor/symbol that serves as a warning to humanity on the road to self-destruction

Summary:
The Doomsday clock has been in existence since 1947 when the threat that nuclear warfare became real. The cook was introduced as a metaphor to show how critical the situation is, with midnight as Doomsday. The time to midnight is re-assessed every year in the light of nuclear and other threats. Lately, the issue of climate change has also been factored into the scenario. With growing unease between major geopolitical players, new ballistic missile developments by the US and Russia and a growing climate change crisis, the clock was set at 100 seconds to midnight in January this year -- before the pandemic.

Further information:
On Thursday, 23 January 2020, the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, which takes stock of the threats posed by nuclear war and climate change each year, moved the Doomsday Clock to 100 seconds before midnight. The Doomsday Clock is a symbol that represents the likelihood of a man-made global catastrophe. The Clock is a metaphor for threats to humanity from unchecked scientific and technical advances. It represents the hypothetical global catastrophe as "midnight" and the Bulletin's opinion on how close the world is to a global catastrophe as a number of "minutes" to midnight, assessed in January of each year. The main factors influencing the Clock are nuclear risk and climate change. The Bulletin's Science and Security Board also monitors new developments in the life sciences and technology that could inflict irrevocable harm to humanity.

The time of 100 seconds before midnight is the closest to Doomsday we have been since the clock was created in 1947. Given the current state of global affairs, it is hard to imagine that in the early 1990s, the Doomsday Clock was moved as far away from midnight as 17 minutes.

The actual clock is in Chicago where the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists is located. The Bulletin was founded by those who worked on the Manhattan Project during World War II, now includes 13 Nobel Laureates on the board and a number of Elders. Some really prominent world figures like Ban Ki Moon and Mary Robinson, the former Prime Minister of Ireland are involved and the CEO of the Bulletin can assist in getting interviews with some of them.

Both the Bulletin and the Elders have reacted very positively to our request and we were scheduled to shoot in Chicago and Dublin in April, but the pandemic put a halt to it.

However, then I have approached them again for Skype or Zoom interviews and they are keen to do it.

Mary Robinson is the most difficult one to pin down and she has now agreed to an interview this coming Thursday at 14:00.

The CEO of the Bulletin Rachel Bronson can be available at 15:30 our time this coming Thursday.

While we are living outa doomsday scenario, it would interesting to get their take on things, the clock the pandemic and the fragility of human existence that has become so apparent in recent weeks.

We will also interview a South African expert -- perhaps a trends analyst like Dion Chang.

Press Release:


What Will it Take to Reset the Doomsday Clock?
Will I stay at home and social distance? Will I burn fossil fuel? Scientists say that with manmade disasters piling up, mankind’s hurtling down the path of self-destruction. They believe humanity is closer than ever before to doomsday and has set the metaphorical Doomsday Clock to only 100 seconds to midnight – an indication that the threat level is critical. However, they also say that every right choice from individuals to global leaders can make a difference to the fate of the world. The metaphorical clock is set and maintained by the Bulletin of Atomic Scientists in the United States. Their Doomsday Clock was devised in 1947 as a tool to warn and encourage wiser choices. Carte Blanche asks if there’s still time to change?
Producer: Eugene Botha | Presenter: Derek Watts


Script:


V/O:
Science fiction writers love Doomsday scenarios. Nuclear warheads creating mushroom clouds…. A climate out of control…a man-made killer contagion leaving cities deserted….. But all of this seemed unreal and extremely far away…. until three months ago.
LINK: (Mask and sanitizer)
With the Coronavirus putting billions of people in lockdown, what was once just science fiction has become all too real. And it makes one think that other doomsday scenarios are perhaps also not just science fiction.
V/O:
In the United States, A Doomsday Clock has recently issued an apocalypse alert. And it is no joke -- some of the world's leading scientists are involved with this clock, and they all think Doomsday is a real possibility and closer than ever before.

However, the Doomsday Clock is not trying to predict precisely how and when the end will come. It is rather a metaphor of how close we are to a human-made global catastrophe, a warning that humans by their careless actions and technology are jeopardizing their existence. The clock is a symbol, a warning to everybody, especially world leaders, of how imminent humanity's self-destruction is.

On the clock face midnight equals Doomsday, and the closer the minute hand is to 12, the closer humanity is to self-destruction.

The clock is reset every year, and over the years, the position of the minute hand has fluctuated, indicating if the threat to humanity is increasing or decreasing.
LINK:
This year, on the 23rd of January when the new setting of the clock was revealed it was a shocker. The arms of the clock were moved to only 100 seconds before midnight.
V/O:
It is the closest the hands of the clock have ever been to Doomsday.

Rachel Bronson is the CEO of the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, an organization that created the idea of the clock.
Derek:
Rachel, is it a physical clock?

Rachel:
We do have a physical clock and we have had different clocks through the years, but it is really more of an idea.
V/O:
Prof Brett Bennett is an historian at the University of Johannesburg.
Barrett:
The Doomsday Clock was created out of the Manhattan Project which was the basis of the American atomic programme and some of the scientists became very much alarmed at the potential implications for the world.
V/O:
They decided to create a mechanism to communicate their concern to the public. This led to the creation of the Doomsday clock.

In 1953 the clock was set at just 2 minutes before midnight because of the advent of thermo-nuclear weapons much more powerful than atomic bombs.
Barrett:
This was a massive game changer. This indicated destruction at a level humans had hitherto never imagined.
V/O:
When the cold war ended in 1991 the clock was set back to 17 minutes to midnight.It was a safer time.
LINK:
The settings of the clock are not decided upon arbitrarily. A significant number of factors are taken into consideration when deciding on how close we are to midnight.
V/O:
When the clock was launched, the main issue was the threat of nuclear war. However, at present, the threats of climate change, disruptive technologies, a worldwide leadership crisis, and lack of respect for science are also factored into the settings.

This year Mary Robinson was invited to the unveiling. She is a former prime minister of Ireland, and also served as United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. She is currently the President of the Elders, an international organisation consisting of elder statesmen, peace activists, and human rights advocates.
Mary:
I was very honoured to be asked in 2007 to be a founder member of the Elders a gropup that Nelson Mandela was brining together to help him to promote the values that he stood for,.
V/O:
Both Robinson and another Elder Ban Ki-Moon were involved this year when the latest Doomsday Clock setting took place.
Derek:
Mary, the clock was set at 100 seconds to midnight in January. Is the threat really so imminent?
Mary:
That is what the scientists explained. This is not opinion this is actually scientific analysis. And the two issues that there were particularly focused on were the nuclear issue which was going backwards. And secondly climate change that was not improving. And they referenced pandemic nut it was way down the list, it was not a reality.
V/O:
The scientists collaborating on the setting of the clock include some of the leading researhcers in the world.
Rachel:
They come together each year in Chicago and they begin their conversation in November and continue on through January when we announce the time in Washington, DC.
LINK:
When the latest setting of the clock was unveiled one of the reasons for the setting so close to midnight was the agreement among scientists that the world is ill prepared for a global catastrophe.
V/O:
And as COVID-19 proved – they were right. The world was nowhere near prepared for a global pandemic.
Derek:
Must we really think the unthinkable in terms of possible catastrophes?

Rachel:
I think it is important to think about the unthinkable to ensure that they don’t happen. Who would have thought that a pandemic would keep us all in our homes and collapse the international economy. We have to think about it so that we can be better prepared.. If we do not believe climate change is really happening, we won’t make the necessary investment. Preparation is always cheaper than reaction.
V/O:
However, as an historian, Professor Bennett has been somewhat critical of the current setting of the clock.
Derek:
Do you think it is a useful metaphor?

Brett:
It is a useful one because it shows people that we need to act to save the earth and make sure that our living conditions are good. At the same time, I do believe that people can create a sense of panic .and people think, there is not enough time to act. And I think we need to have faith that we do have enough time to act, but we do need to act now.
V/O:
A serious concern that influenced the setting of the clock, is the exponential worldwide increase in Fake News.
Mary:
There will be a reckoning of all of this and we will actually see very visibly the harm of fake news .It kills people. It will kill people during Covic-19. That’s the truth. And this will be very good facts and science and for journalism. For journalism based on facts, which I know Carte Blanche is.
LINK:
When we look at what is happening all around us on a global scale, the obvious question is: how can we as individuals hope to make a difference?
Rachel:
What we are learning from the pandemic is that individual actions make a huge difference, juts staying at home, we see that individuals actions whether it is marches or making your house more environmentally friendly, it all has important consequences, and it put pressure on political leaders.
V/O:
The pandemic has highlighted another essential principle behind the Doomsday Clock
Mary:
It is really important that we recognize that science matters. Health advice from experts matters. If only we will apply that in the future more to climate and particularly in the United States you have climate denial, which is ridiculous, it is very real. Now we have learned that science matters. And government matters, leadership matters. You have good leadership in President Ramaphosa. I gather he was juts praised by the WHO.
Derek:
Difficult to predict but how do you see the setting of the clock next year?

Rachel:
The science and security Board of the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists is regularly thinking about the challenges we face, and what that means for humanity’s safety. We have just issued a statement; we are not bullish about where we are right now. But if this pandemic serves as a wake-up call and drives leaders in a direction to take these issues seriously – the global pandemic, climate change, the nuclear issue. If we see a more urgent response from them, we will happily move the clock further away from midnight.

Derek:
And that would be good news.

Rachel:
And that would be very good news.

The Bulletin was founded by those who worked on the Manhattan Project during World War II, now includes 13 Nobel Laureates on the board and a number of Elders. Some really prominent world figures like Ban Ki Moon and Mary Robinson, the former Prime Minister of Ireland are involved and the CEO of the Bulletin can assist in getting interviews with some of them. Both the Bulletin and the Elders have reacted very positively to our request and we were scheduled to shoot in Chicago and Dublin in April, but the pandemic put a halt to it. However, then I have approached them again for Skype or Zoom interviews and they are keen to do it. Mary Robinson is the most difficult one to pin down and she has now agreed to an interview this coming Thursday at 14:00. The CEO of the Bulletin Rachel Bronson can be available at 15:30 our time this coming Thursday. While we are living outa doomsday scenario, it would interesting to get their take on things, the clock the pandemic and the fragility of human existence that has become so apparent in recent weeks. We will also interview a South African expert -- perhaps a trends analyst like Dion Chang.
